14.text_clean:
14. Two point sources of light have an angular separation of $\theta$, as measured by a distant observer. The light passes through a circular aperture of radius $r$ just before reaching the observer. Which of the following conditions must be true for the two sources to be resolved?
A. $\theta < 0.61\frac{\lambda}{r}$
B. $\theta < 1.22\frac{\lambda}{r}$
C. $\theta \ge 0.61\frac{\lambda}{r}$
D. $\theta \ge 1.22\frac{\lambda}{r}$
14.note: Official key D. The Rayleigh criterion is theta >= 1.22 lambda/b with b the aperture DIAMETER; the question gives the RADIUS r, so b = 2r and the condition is theta >= 0.61 lambda/r, i.e. C. The key appears to treat r as the diameter.
